evidence.C1: Covers all main attack classes (HB101-106 hidden content, HB201-206 injection, HB301/310/311 secrets, HB401-405 execution/exfil, HB501-506 MCP config, HB601-603 tool manifest, HB701 scope, HB801-802 lock); runtime tool-call gate via `check-call`/`check-output`; rug-pull pinning via `hexbane lock`; decoded payloads shown ('hidden text: Ignore all previous instructions.'); measured on Invariant Labs PoCs (3/3 FAIL), anthropics/skills (273 files), MCP servers (388 files). Minor gaps: chat gate 'about 1 in 5 cleverly phrased off-topic requests still gets through' and disguise misses on uniform spacing.
evidence.C2: Zero-install browser scan ('It runs in your browser; your files are never uploaded'); folder drop with 'Choose folder'/'Choose files'; samples ('Poisoned MCP tool', 'Skill with hidden text', 'Disguised instructions', 'Risky MCP config', 'Clean skill'); SARIF output (`--format sarif`); full GitHub Action with `action.yml`; copy-paste fixes per finding; suppressions via `<!-- hexbane-ignore-next-line: HB401 -->`; phone screenshot included; autofix via `hexbane fix`.
evidence.C3: Single brand Hexbane with hex logo; shared navigation (Scan, Chat gate, Dashboard, Policy, Accuracy, Integrate); unified story ('Breaks the hex before your AI agent falls for it'); three gates (load/call/chat) unified under one model; shared `rules.json` across CLI/server/browser; OpenAI-compatible proxy combines all gates; Background section explicitly explains the merge: 'the same attack - instructions smuggled into text an AI reads - shows up at all three moments'.
evidence.C4: Tuning (31), held-out (16), disguised (65), and public sets (273 skills, 388 servers, 3 Invariant PoCs) clearly separated; false alarms individually explained ('False alarm: it tells the agent *never* to run a page's setup scripts and quotes `curl ... | sh` as the bad example'); held-out miss reported honestly ('h07-zed-config... got REVIEW instead of FAIL - left as is, not tuned'); limits stated plainly ('It is a pattern and structure scanner, not a model'); sources linked (Invariant Labs, anthropics/skills, MCP servers); speed measurements included; 'Working prototype by one developer. Not audited.'
evidence.C5: Distinctive hex logo and dark security-tool aesthetic; clear hierarchy with numbered gates (1, 2, 3); severity colors visible (HIGH in red/orange); 'HEXBANE DECODED THE HIDDEN TEXT' callout for disguised text; phone screenshot shows mobile layout works. Cannot verify light theme readability - all provided screenshots are dark-only, and rubric level 7 requires 'readable in both themes'.

fixes: Improve chat gate accuracy: README admits 'about 1 in 5 cleverly phrased off-topic requests still gets through' - this is the weakest measured number and undermines the unified 'stay in scope' story.

Close disguise-handling gaps: uniform spacing only partly recovered (8/14 rules) and spaced command flags slip through (m22-file-upload misses both versions) - the unfolding pass is the headline v2 feature and still has measurable holes.

Add and verify a light theme: all provided screenshots are dark-only; rubric level 7 requires readability in both themes, and a security tool used in code-review contexts will be viewed in light mode by many developers.

evidence.C1: All four 10-anchor pieces present: 'Call gate | every tool call and tool result at run time | allow/ask/deny', 'hexbane lock ... flags anything that changed (rug pull)', decoded payload shown ('hidden text: Ignore all previous instructions.'), and measured public-sample results (3/3 Invariant PoCs, 273+388-file scans with per-file alarm review). Docked because the runtime half is unmeasured: call gate has no numbers and the chat-gate figure lives only 'in the app's Accuracy tab'.
evidence.C2: Every 10-anchor item evidenced: zero-install browser scan ('paste or drop a SKILL.md ... It runs in your browser; your files are never uploaded') with folder drop and 5 samples; SARIF ('--format sarif') plus a full composite action.yml; 'copy-paste fix for that exact file and line' with suppression syntax and browser 'False alarm? Mark it as reviewed'.
evidence.C3: One brand and one model: 'the same attack ... shows up at all three moments: when a tool is loaded, when it runs, and when a user types'; UI numbers the gates 1-2-3; 'stay in scope' applied to skills (HB701 'Skill does more than it says') and chat ('keeps a business assistant on its mission'). Docked: chat-gate heuristics sit outside the 32 shared rules and the Policy tab is never explained.
evidence.C4: Exemplary separation: tuning (31, 'rules were tuned on it') vs held-out (16, 'run once') vs public folders; 'Every non-PASS file is listed' with fair/unfair verdicts; blunt limits ('not a benchmark', 'Not audited', paraphrase gap); pinned sources (@7382a5e, @2c5958e). Docked: chat-gate accuracy (~1 in 5 bypass) referenced to the app tab rather than tabulated with sample sizes.
evidence.C5: Desktop dark UI is clean and hierarchical (FAIL banner, HIGH chips, decoded-text callout, why/fix structure), but both phone screenshots truncate the nav at 'Accur', no light theme is shown, and the small red decoded-text callout's contrast is unverified.

fixes: Fix the phone layout: the top nav is cut off at 'Accur' in both mobile screenshots (wrap or collapse it), and publish light-theme screenshots with contrast-checked severity colours to evidence the 10 anchor.

Add measured runtime-gate numbers with sample sizes to docs/EVALUATION.md - the call gate has no published deny/quarantine rate and the chat-gate '~1 in 5' bypass figure lives only in the app's Accuracy tab.

Fold the chat-gate heuristics into the shared rules.json (or explain the split) and document the Policy tab in the README so load/call/chat read as one rule system rather than scanner plus bolted-on gate.
